title: Nous Research raises $90M to take its Hermes AI agent to businesses
source_used: The Next Web (citing The Wall Street Journal)
key_facts: Nous Research raised $90 million to build a business version of Hermes, its open-source AI agent.
Investors include Nvidia, Microsoft's M12, Samsung, Robot Ventures, Union Square Ventures, Y Combinator and Menlo Ventures, per CEO Dillon Rolnick's note on the company website.
The Wall Street Journal, which first broke the news, reported a valuation of $1.5 billion; Nous did not give a valuation.
Nous released Hermes under the MIT licence in February; it remembers projects, writes reusable skills and lets users choose models.
Nous says Hermes has been cloned more than 24 million times and drives about 2.5% of global token use by its own estimate; the Journal reported more than 22 million downloads since February.
The money goes into 'Hermes for Businesses', which will let companies choose models by price and goal, keep AI use private and own their company knowledge.
quote_evidence: Nous Research has raised $90M to build a business version of Hermes, its open-source AI agent.
The round values Nous at $1.5bn, The Wall Street Journal reported, which first broke the news.
why_it_matters_hint: An open-source agent with large claimed usage is moving into the business market.
